explicit_definitions_given: Ethics: moral action and provisional code
Will: ability to do or not do something

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Acknowledges Descartes' explicit intention but shows internal contradictions
objections_raised: Descartes explicitly subordinates ethics to philosophy
Descartes defines ego as thinking thing, excluding action

summary_of_core_decisions: The article argues that Descartes' separation of philosophy and ethics, with philosophy primary, is reversed in his own texts. Four arguments show ethics' priority: (1) moral action cannot be suspended, (2) the fourth moral maxim commands philosophizing, (3) will (ethics) is prior and more authoritative than intellect (philosophy) in error and judgment, (4) the ego as thinking thing is incomplete because willing is essentially acting. Thus, ethics is fundamental and the ego is a morally-acting substance.
